description_full: Amalgamated Financial Corp. operates as the bank holding company for Amalgamated Bank that provides commercial and retail banking, investment management, and trust and custody services in the United States. It accepts various deposit products, including non-interest-bearing accounts, interest-bearing demand products, savings accounts, money market accounts, NOW accounts, time deposits, and certificates of deposit. The company also provides commercial and industrial, multifamily mortgage, commercial real estate, residential real estate mortgage, consumer solar, and consumer and other loans. In addition, it offers online banking, bill payment, online cash management, safe deposit box rentals, debit card, and ATM card services; and trust, custody, and investment management services, including asset safekeeping, corporate actions, income collections, proxy services, account transition, asset transfers, and conversion management. Further, the company provides investment products, such as index and actively-managed funds, which include equity, fixed-income, real estate, and alternative investments; and investment, brokerage, asset management, and insurance products, as well as lending services. Amalgamated Financial Corp. was founded in 1923 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

financial_summary: Amalgamated Financial Corp. is a small-cap financial services business with a $1.5B market cap on $329M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are expanding by +2.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 19% against a 8% cost of capital — a 10-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $134M in free cash flow — roughly 41 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.30× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 1.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 37% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
